## Satisfaction and Income/Wealth Association

The merged table uses the earliest matched observation in each two-year ESS
round and the corresponding WID distribution. It retains ESS reliability,
effective sample size, the selected post-tax income series where available,
and WID extrapolation flags. The full country-round table is available as
[data/processed/ess_wid_country_round.csv](data/processed/ess_wid_country_round.csv).

All summaries and correlations below use ESS observations flagged reliable.
Correlations are descriptive only; no significance tests are performed. Gini
values are approximated from WID's ten decile shares. Palma is the top 10% share
divided by the bottom 40% share; wealth Palma is missing when bottom-40 net wealth
is zero or negative.

### Variance Decomposition

Between-country and within-country percentages describe where the reliable
country-round variation in each measure occurs.

```{r}
#| label: association-variance-decomposition
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(analysis$association$variance, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Measure Selection

The following selections apply to exploratory scatterplot selection and variance
decomposition. The compact regime comparison below uses mean satisfaction only.

```{r}
#| label: association-measure-selection
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  analysis$association$measure_selection,
  col.names = c("Satisfaction measure", "Correlations", "Variance decomposition"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

### Between-Country Association

Each point is a country's mean across reliable survey rounds. The two panels compare
mean economic satisfaction with the corresponding income or wealth Gini. Only a
few extreme points are labeled to keep the scatter readable.

```{r}
#| label: association-between-country
#| echo: false
knitr::include_graphics(analysis$association$plot_files[["between"]])
```

### Within-Country Association

Values are demeaned within each country, separating changes over time from
persistent differences between countries.

```{r}
#| label: association-within-country
#| echo: false
knitr::include_graphics(analysis$association$plot_files[["within"]])
```

### Satisfaction by Year

The line shows the reliable cross-country mean by year; the band spans the
cross-country 25th to 75th percentiles. Larger points indicate more reliable
country observations in that year.

```{r}
#| label: association-year-pattern
#| echo: false
knitr::include_graphics(analysis$association$plot_files[["year_patterns"]])
```

### Selected Correlation Scatterplots

These pooled country-round comparisons show the three distribution metrics in each
domain with the largest absolute Spearman correlations. Each metric is paired with
its strongest selected satisfaction summary. Wealth middle-40% and income bottom-50%
shares are always included when a usable pairing exists. The table identifies the
actual measures selected; share axes are percentages.

Selection is exploratory, not evidence of statistical significance or causation.
Countries contribute repeated observations, so these pooled correlations combine
between-country differences with changes over time. Each point is a reliable
country-round; red lines are descriptive ordinary least-squares fits.

```{r}
#| label: association-selected-pairs
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  analysis$association$selected_associations[c(
    "distribution_label", "satisfaction_label", "n", "countries", "pearson", "spearman"
  )],
  col.names = c("Distribution measure", "Satisfaction measure", "Rounds", "Countries",
                "Pearson", "Spearman"),
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE
)
```

### Middle-40% Wealth and Mean Satisfaction by Welfare Regime

This compact table examines only **middle-40% wealth share (WID)** versus
**mean economic satisfaction (ESS)**. Same-source correlations and the full
correlation matrices are omitted. Welfare regime and Post-Communist status are
shown together, using the fixed country labels in `esping_typology_simple.csv`;
the extended labels are not all original Esping-Andersen categories.

The Post-Communist regime row also supplies the Post-Communist aggregate.
The final row pools all other classified regimes for comparison, without
repeating the Post-Communist result. Unknown classifications remain separate,
not assumed non-Post-Communist. The aggregate rows overlap the regime rows
and are not additional independent samples.

Coefficients use finite pairs from reliable country-rounds; fewer than three
pairs or a constant measure produces an unavailable coefficient. Empty
categories remain visible. These pooled correlations mix country differences
and changes over time, and countries with more rounds contribute more pairs.
A one-country category describes only that country's series. Differences
between coefficients are descriptive, not significance tests or causal regime
effects; the non-Post-Communist aggregate combines heterogeneous regimes.

```{r}
#| label: association-focused-wealth-correlations
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  analysis$association$focused_wealth_correlations[c(
    "welfare_regime", "post_communist_status", "n", "countries",
    "pearson", "spearman", "status"
  )],
  col.names = c("Welfare regime / sample", "Post-Communist status", "Paired rounds",
                "Countries", "Pearson", "Spearman", "Availability"),
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE
)
```
